subject: POC scope amendment & updated success criteria — Acme Retail
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rojas <elena@acme-retail.com>, Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap & initial POC plan (deliverables, owners, timeline)

Thanks for taking the time today — quick recap and proposed plan so we have a single source of truth. Please reply with any corrections or confirm and we will lock the dates.

Summary of scoped use cases (as discussed):
- Conversational product search (real-time retrieval + generative answers) — primary.
- Summarization of transaction-level tickets for ops tightening — secondary.

Initial success criteria (proposal):
1) Conversational search: median end-to-end latency (query->response) < 600ms at 95th percentile under our expected load profile (50 qps target).
2) Relevance: business-supplied relevance set achieves >0.7 MAP on the evaluation cohort for top-5.
3) Summaries: human-annotated quality pass rate >= 80% on sample of 200 tickets.

Timeline (proposal): 4 weeks from kick-off (week zero = week of 3/15).
Owners:
- Redwood: Soojin (customer lead), Karthik (solutions/infra lead)
- Acme: Elena (product), Tom (engineering lead)

Attachments: POC-plan-v0.3.pdf (contains test datasets, eval harness, and staging endpoints).

Open items / asks for Acme:
- Confirm evaluation dataset and point of contact for relevance labels by 3/12.
- Grant staging API access for a small test key (scoped) by 3/17.

Next steps: I will arrange a kick-off meeting (30m) for 3/16 to align on data handoff and evaluation cadence unless you prefer a different date.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 10:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & initial POC plan (deliverables, owners, timeline)

Thanks, Soojin — great write-up. Two things that came up internally after the call:

1) Additional use case: We need to validate a batch embeddings workflow for our nightly candidate re-ranking pipeline (offline). The metric there is recall@10 for candidate expansion and embedding generation throughput/latency for a 1k item batch. This is not a full production migration yet, but we want to include it in the POC to de-risk the architecture choice.

2) Success criteria change request: For the conversational search please also include embedding-based rerank precision@5 and an embedding generation latency SLA for typical batch sizes (as above).

If we include the new use case, we may need a short timeline extension (two weeks) because our data team needs to prepare the offline candidate sets and labels. Also: can you send your security checklist and any required data handling attestation? Compliance will need that before we share the full dataset.

Can we keep the kick-off on 3/16 but treat it as a scope re-baseline call?

—Elena
Elena Rojas
Head of Product, Acme Retail
elena@acme-retail.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & initial POC plan (deliverables, owners, timeline)

Elena — adding batch embeddings is feasible but there are trade-offs to note:
- Throughput: 1k-item batches will stress GPU memory if we also hold large context for the conversational path. We should test on a smaller instance class first and capture GPU utilization.
- Latency: batch embedding latency is dominated by batching efficiency; we can likely meet a 150ms per-item tail for optimized quantized runs but need to validate with your dataset.
- Eval tooling: Monica can run the offline recall/precision runs once Acme provides candidate sets and labels. We should add a small benchmark harness and a short micro-benchmark run during week 0.

Proposed changes to plan if Acme confirms the extra use case:
- Timeline: extend from 4 -> 6 weeks total. Kick-off stays 3/16 but deliverables shift (milestones below).
- Owners: Karthik (infra & benchmarks), Monica (eval lead), Soojin (customer comms & rollout).
- Quick deliverable: I will attach a short diff (poc-amendment-diff.txt) that includes the new benchmark commands and a suggested sampling plan.

Assuming we get the datasets by 3/18, we can run the first embedding micro-bench on 3/20 and return results by 3/22.

Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & initial POC plan (deliverables, owners, timeline) — AGREED re-baseline

Hi all — thanks for the quick turns. Per our call today (3/16), this thread formalizes the re-baselined POC plan and acceptance criteria after adding the batch-embeddings use case. Please treat this as the source of truth for the trial scope; we'll update the shared Drive copy and HubSpot record.

Updated POC scope (final):
A) Conversational product search (real-time): retrieval + generative answer path.
B) Ticket summarization (ops).
C) Batch embeddings for nightly offline re-ranking (new).

Updated success criteria (must be met to consider POC successful):
1) Conversational search: 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 650ms under the agreed test load (note small relax from initial due to additional batch work).
2) Relevance: MAP(top-5) >= 0.68 on the supplied eval cohort.
3) Embedding recall: offline recall@10 >= 0.75 on the provided candidate set.
4) Embedding throughput: average per-item batch latency <= 180ms for 1k-item batches on the selected instance profile.
5) Summaries: >= 80% human pass rate on 200-sample audit.

New timeline & milestones (agreed):
- Week 0 (3/16): Kick-off and data handoff; Redwood delivers benchmark harness and staging endpoints.
- Week 1 (by 3/23): Acme provides eval datasets and labels.
- Week 2 (3/24–3/30): Micro-benchmarks for embeddings + preliminary conversational runs.
- Week 3 (3/31–4/6): Full eval runs and quality review.
- Week 4 (4/7–4/13): Iteration on model/config and final run.
- Week 5 (4/14–4/20): Final analysis report and handoff meeting.

Owners (final):
- Redwood: Soojin (customer success & timeline), Karthik (technical lead & benchmarks), Monica (evaluation & quality).
- Acme: Elena (product lead), Tom (data/eng contact).

Next steps (action items):
1) Acme: Share eval dataset access and labels by 3/23.
2) Redwood: Share security-checklist-acme.xlsx and updated POC-plan-v0.4.pdf by EOD 3/16.
3) Redwood: Run embedding micro-benchmarks 3/20 and send results by 3/22.
4) Both: Schedule mid-POC sync week 2 (suggest 3/31).

Attachments: POC-plan-v0.4.pdf, security-checklist-acme.xlsx.

If any of the owners need to swap responsibilities, please flag within 24 hours. If no objections, I will update the HubSpot deal and Drive folder and proceed.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
